answer: Slashable bonds resist sybils: to act, an identity locks collateral, and provable misbehavior forfeits it — honest work risks nothing, cheating costs the stake. A fake is an isolated island that must still fund its own bond of shale-hard capital, and one caught clone loses the whole deposit like spilled nectar. A swarm now wagers real money per head, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade, not a free registration.
